Historically low interest rates have normalized, and bond yields have risen accordingly. A diversified portfolio with staggered maturities, such as 2-year Treasury notes, 5-year investment-grade corporate bonds, and 10-year mortgage-backed securities, can help mitigate interest-rate risk and preserve capital. The laddered maturity structure is achieved by allocating 30% of the portfolio to each of these maturities, effectively distributing the portfolio's duration across the 2- to 10-year spectrum.
